entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: MFA No.20554/2012 is filed by the insurance company questioning the judgment and award dated 02.11.2011 in MVC No.1893/2009 alleging that the auto rickshaw bearing No.MH_01/H-2652 is not involved in the accident.

3. It is the case of the claimant that on 29.08.2009 at about 12 noon, he was pedestrian on the left side of the road and at that time one goods auto rickshaw bearing No.MH-01-H-2652 has dashed the claimant, due to which claimant had sustained injuries.
Therefore, claimant filed claim petition.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
5.

The counsel for the insurance company submitted that the auto rickshaw bearing No.MH-01-H-2652 is not NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 involved in the accident and falsely implicated in the case as the claimant has sustained the injuries by falling in the home.
Therefore, the injuries sustained in the home is converted into road traffic accident and he placed reliance on the Ex.P18-evidence of doctor-PW4.
Therefore, prays to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. Further, submitted that complaint is lodged after 10 days from the date of accident and therefore the auto rickshaw No.MH-01-H-2652 was falsely mentioned in the complaint and manipulation was done just to make claim against the insurance company.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant was dashed by the auto rickshaw and it was reflected as road traffic accident in the medical records of Belagavi Institute of Medical Sciences and Vijayanagar hospital.
Therefore, submitted that, it is a road traffic accident that the claimant suffered NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 injuries and it is rightly considered by the Tribunal.
Hence, prays to allow the appeal.

The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Devappa Vasu Bandurge on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178048902/
3 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No doubt, the complaint is lodged after 10 days from the date of accident.
On 29.08.2009 accident was occurred.
Whereas, admittedly complaint is lodged on 07.09.2009.
Just because there is a delay in lodging the complaint is not always a ground to reject the claim petition.
In the present case, on 29.08.2009, the claimant had sustained injuries and on the same day, admitted to the Tukkar Hospital, Belagavi.
On the next day i.e. on 30.08.2009, the claimant was discharged from the Tukkar Hospital and admitted to the Belagavi Institute of Medical Sciences.
Then, the claimant was admitted to Vijaya Hospital, Belagavi.
9. Ex.P.18 is not the case sheet, it is only a receipt of reimbursable/non-reimbursable bill and nothing more than that.
In the Ex.P.18, it is stated that fall at home.

Even though, the PW.4 has stated that in Ex.P.18 is written as"
fall at home" whatever PW.4 has given evidence is based NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 on Ex.P.18-bill.
Whereas, on the next date on 30.08.2009, claimant was admitted to BIMS hospital, Belagavi wherein, it is mentioned that the claimant has met with road traffic accident and sustained injuries.
Then, the claimant admitted to the Vijay hospital, Belagavi wherein also history is shown as road traffic accident.
The medical records of BIMS and Vijaya hospital prove that the claimant has sustained injuries due to road traffic accident.
PWs.5 and 6 are the doctors of BIMS hospital and Vijaya hospital.
They have stated that the claimant was admitted in the hospital with a history of road traffic accident.
In the case sheet of BIMS and Vijaya hospital, it is stated that on 30.08.2009, the claimant had admitted in the hospital wherein the history is road traffic accident.
10. The evidence of doctor PWs.5 and 6 go to prove that the claimant was admitted to hospital with a history of road traffic accident.
Only, PW.4 has deposed in EX.P18- receipt in which it is stated that "fall at home".

Therefore, the entire evidence on record is considered, case sheet NC:
2023:KHC-D:10851 from Tukkar hospital is not produced but, Ex.P18 is the only receipt in which it is written as "fall at home".
Quite naturally, PW.4 doctor has stated on the face of Ex.P18, that the claimant had sustained injuries due to fall at home.
But, whereas, the case sheet and other medical records produced by the BIMS and Vijaya Hospital, the claimant was admitted to the hospital with a history of road traffic accident.

Therefore, the case sheet produced by BIMS and Vijaya Hospital,
Belagavi are not be stated that they are manipulated.

Therefore, when considering the case on its merits in the absence of case sheet of Tukkar Hospital by only Ex.P18-receipt, it cannot be stated that the claimant had not met with road traffic accident.
Therefore, from the case sheets of BIMS and Vijay hospital compared to evidence of doctors, the claimant was admitted to hospital with a history of accident when he was dashed by auto rickshaw.

In this regard, the Tribunal has rightly considered the evidence on record and held that the claimant had met with accident through auto rickshaw and therefore, the claimant has awarded with NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 compensation.
In this regard, the finding of fact assigned by the Tribunal cannot be interfered with.

11. Considering the nature of injuries sustained that the claimant had suffered fracture of right patella and the claimant was in hospital only for a period of two days, the compensation amount awarded by the tribunal is found to be just and proper.

sentences.text: In so far as, compensation on the heads pain and suffering, medical expenses, incidental expenses, loss of earning during treatment are found to be correct.

The Tribunal has taken only 8%
functional disability.
The claimant had a grocery business shop.
Therefore, fracture to the right patella certainly causes a difficulty in earning, livelihood for doing grocery business.
It is just and proper to take 10% as functional disability.

The doctor has stated that claimant had suffered 20%
disability considering the nature of injury sustained.
13. The accident is of the year 2009, the notional income is Rs.5,000/- p.m.
The age of the claimant is 55 years and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 appropriate multiplier is 11.

Hence, loss of earning capacity due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as below:
Rs.5,000/-X10/100X11X12=Rs.66,000/-.
14.
Further, a compensation of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head loss of amenities.
15. Thus, in all claimant is entitled for the compensation as awarded by this Court
is as follows:

Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Loss of earning capacity due to 66,000-00  disability  2. Towards loss of amenities.
3. Medical expenses 13,000-00  4
Towards nursing attendant 5,000-00  charges, conveyance extra  nourishment  5 Loss of earning during treatment 5,000-00

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,19,000/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10851 realization, as against Rs.95,000-00 awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

17. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

ii) The judgment and award dated 02.11.2011, passed by the Fast Track III and MACT, Belgaum, in MVC No.1893/2009 stands modified.

iii) Appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed in part since the interest is scaled down from 8% p.a. to 6% p.a.
iv) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs. 1,19,000/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (Tribunal has awarded interest at 8% and the same is scaled down to 6%) from the date of petition till its realization.
The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vi) Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
